hints: The product of everything except index i splits into two parts: everything before i and everything after i. Can you get both parts quickly for every i?
Use prefix and suffix products. First fill the answer with the product of everything to the left, then sweep from the right multiplying in a running suffix product.

1. Create res of size n; set res[0] = 1.
  2. Left to right: res[i] = res[i-1] * nums[i-1] (product of the left part).
  3. Set suffix = 1.
  4. Right to left: res[i] *= suffix, then suffix *= nums[i].
  5. Return res.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each index, multiply all other elements.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Build separate prefix and suffix product arrays and multiply them.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Store prefix products in the output array, then fold in the suffix with a single variable.

explain: For [2,3,1,5]: the left pass gives [1,2,6,6]. The right pass multiplies by suffix 1, 5, 5, 15, giving [15,10,30,6]. Each position ends up with (product before it) × (product after it), never touching itself, so no division is needed. This also handles zeros correctly, as in [-1,0,4], where dividing would break.
recognize: 'Product of all except self' without division → prefix × suffix products.
python:
class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums); out = [1] * n; p = 1
        for i in range(n): out[i] = p; p *= nums[i]
        p = 1
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1): out[i] *= p; p *= nums[i]
        return out
